A skip reconnects node 2 to the input, gaining more than replacing a working op.

Removing a strong direct edge hurts far more than removing a weak one.
A skip adds a useful residual path where none existed.
A skip fills an empty edge with an easy-to-train path, which is worth more than replacing an existing op.
Removing a strong conv edge costs more accuracy than removing a weak op.
